name: is_allowlisted
note: Called by apps/web/src/middleware.ts on every protected request. If this is missing or its grant is wrong, every employee hits /access-denied with gate_unavailable. Granted to authenticated only, so anon must be denied.

name: auth_user_with_allowlist
note: The Worker's jwtAuth middleware calls this on every authenticated API request. service_role only. Probed with p_user_id because an empty body returns PGRST202, which is indistinguishable from the function being absent.

name: bid_recording_coverage
note: DROPPED by migration 20260930120000, and this entry is now the guard that it stays dropped (#1466). It was the first per workflow bid recording comparison (#1157); bid_recording_coverage_v2 replaced it for both the daily bid-recording check and the too few bids monitor, and the original was kept one release for rollback per ADR 0007. Probed with both args so the shape still matches the signature that existed, because a probe with the wrong args answers PGRST202 too and would report absence it never measured.

name: bid_recording_coverage_v2
note: bid_recording_coverage plus attempt_rows (#1413), read by the daily bid-recording check and the too few bids monitor as service_role. Same SECURITY DEFINER shape as the original, so anon must never reach it. Probed with both args because an empty body returns PGRST202, which is indistinguishable from the function being absent.

name: bid_recording_coverage_v3
note: bid_recording_coverage_v2 over a window with an end (#1929), read by the too few bids monitor as service_role over a day ending ten minutes ago. Same SECURITY DEFINER shape as v2, so anon must never reach it. Probed with all three args because a probe with the wrong args answers PGRST202, which is indistinguishable from the function being absent.

name: email_drop_counts_by_source
note: Aggregates leads whose email Salesforce rejected, per source (#744). Read by the daily email-drop-rate check in the Worker as service_role. Takes the organization as a parameter and is SECURITY DEFINER, so anon must never reach it.

name: field_presence_window
note: Called hourly by the Tier-1 field presence drought check (#1101) for the trailing window it judges. If this is missing the check throws rather than reporting an all-clear, so the failure is loud, but the drought alert stops working entirely until it is restored. Granted to service_role only, so anon must be denied.

name: unpaginated_big_tables
note: Revoked from anon and authenticated by migration 20260814000002. Called only by the nightly big-table guard in the Worker as service_role. Probed with p_min_rows because an empty body cannot match the signature.

name: user_org_id
reason: Deliberately left callable, documented in migration 20260813000004. 28 RLS policies call it, and a policy whose function the querying role cannot execute ERRORS rather than denying, so revoking it would break the app instead of hardening it. It returns only the caller's own organization from their own JWT, and measured against prod an anonymous caller gets null.

name: drop_expired_execution_partitions
note: DROPPED by migration 20260910220000, and this entry is now the guard that it stays dropped (#1145). It deleted a day of execution history without consulting the archive gate, which is why it went. The reason it is worth asserting LIVE rather than only in migration text: being inert is how a routine like this survives, and the next person looking for the procedure that drops expired partitions finds a name that reads like the right one. A migration scan cannot see one recreated by hand in the database. Probed with p_retention_days so the shape still matches the overload that existed, because a probe with the wrong args answers PGRST202 too and would report absence it never measured. The gated replacements are truncate_verified_execution_partitions and drop_verified_execution_partitions, both PROCEDUREs and so unprobeable here.

name: drain_lead_sightings_purge
note: Deletes exported lead_sightings rows. Row level, so RLS constrained it, but there is no reason a browser role should reach it.

name: pg_cron_health
note: Read hourly by the Worker's pg-cron watch (#770) to see whether the database's own scheduled jobs are failing or have stopped. Security definer, so it MUST be denied to anon: Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function by default, which is #762, and without the REVOKE this hands anybody with the publishable key a listing of every scheduled job and its error messages.

name: query_timeout_watch
note: Read hourly by the Worker's query-timeout watch (#1043) to see which statements are approaching their role's statement_timeout, before one is cancelled with a 57014 (#1040). Security definer, so it MUST be denied to anon: Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function by default (#762), and this discloses the slowest statements and their shapes. Probed with p_min_calls because an empty body returns PGRST202, indistinguishable from the function being absent.

name: archive_index_health
note: Read daily by the Worker (#1044) to confirm the index the archive's per-hour count reads by is present, valid, and attached to every execution_steps partition. Without it that count takes 7.1 seconds warm and times out under load, and an index is a performance property so nothing else reports its absence until a run fails. Security definer, so it MUST be denied to anon: Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function by default (#762), and this discloses the partition layout. Takes defaults, so it probes the real index.

name: stranded_step_partitions
note: Read by the Worker's archive health report (#1249) to name step partitions that exist, are themselves verified, and are held back only because the day before them refuses. The two authorised day lists legitimately differ, so a length comparison cannot report this. Security definer, so it MUST be denied to anon: Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function by default (#762), and this discloses the partition layout.

name: archive_day_measurements
note: The Postgres half of the deletion gate's per-day measurement (#872): execution and step counts, orphan executions, erasures. Read daily by the Worker. Security definer, so it MUST be denied to anon: Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function by default (#762), and this returns volume figures for the whole tenant. Probed with an ancient day so the probe measures nothing.

name: archive_day_probe_sample
note: Picks the executions the deletion gate decompresses and checks (#872), returning their ids and trace ids. Security definer and it hands back identifiers, so anon must be denied. Probed with a sample size of zero so it returns nothing.

name: record_archive_day_measurement
note: Writes a day's gate measurement (#872). A WRITE, so anon reaching it would let anybody fabricate the numbers that authorise deleting a partition once A5 (#873) lands. Probed against 1970-01-01, a day that can never be a deletion candidate, so a successful probe leaves one inert row rather than corrupting a real day.

name: execution_purge_retention
note: The daily retention drift check (lib/retention-check.ts) calls this to read what the two execution purge cron jobs are actually scheduled at, so a hand change to either can be compared against RETENTION_DAYS (#1017). service_role only: anon and authenticated have no business reading the schedule on which production data is destroyed. If it is missing the check alerts that it could not read, which is deliberate, because reporting no differences from a failed read would make a broken check and a healthy system the same output.

name: save_buyer_profile
note: The only writer of a buyer profile (#1409). A WRITE: anon reaching it could enable a buyer or reprice one. Probed with the all zero org and partner, which no row carries, so even a successful probe refuses partner_not_found and writes nothing.

name: save_partner_config
note: The partner save (#2132), the Worker's only partner UPDATE. A WRITE: anon reaching it could switch a partner on or change where leads are posted. Probed with the all zero org and partner, which no row carries, so even a successful probe refuses partner_not_found and writes nothing.

name: save_partner_page
note: The partners page save (#2133): the partner record and the buyer profile in one transaction, behind the Worker's PUT /partners/:id/page. A WRITE: anon reaching it could switch a partner or a buyer on, or reprice one. Probed with the all zero org and partner, which no row carries, so even a successful probe refuses partner_not_found and writes nothing. The page calls this route, so the function must exist before the Worker that serves it deploys.

name: save_partner_page
note: The partners page save with the press's tab (#2135), the eleven argument overload the Worker's PUT /partners/:id/page calls from this release, so the notice it sends carries client_id. A WRITE. Probed with the all zero org and partner, so even a successful probe refuses partner_not_found and writes nothing. The ten argument entry above stays for the release before.

name: _apply_buyer_profile
note: The body of a buyer profile save (#2133), called only by save_buyer_profile and save_partner_page, which hold the row locks and compare the version first. Internal, with no grant to anyone: reached directly it would write a profile with no version check. Probed with the all zero partner, so nothing could be written even if a grant appeared.

name: buyer_profile_document
note: Reads one buyer profile as a document (#1412). STABLE, read only. Probed with the all zero id, which no partner carries, so a successful probe returns null.

name: record_buyer_sale
note: Upserts a buyer_sales row (#1409). A WRITE. Probed with an empty row, which the function refuses as missing_key before touching the table.

name: upsert_buyer_select_parity_day
note: Writes one day's Stage A parity counts and their hash, never a sign off (#1413). A WRITE. Probed with an empty row, which the function refuses as missing_key before touching the table.

name: sign_off_buyer_select_parity_day
note: Records a person's sign off of one parity day against the counts hash they saw (#1413). A WRITE. Probed with the all zero workflow and org, which no row carries, so even a successful probe refuses parity_day_not_found and writes nothing.

name: delete_partner_config
note: Deletes a partner and its sub-account IDs as the delete check reviewed them (#1409, #2140). A WRITE. Probed through the five argument overload the Worker calls since #2140, with the all zero id, which no row carries, so a successful probe refuses partner_not_found. The four argument overload stays for the release before #2140.

name: partner_delete_check
note: What deleting one partner would do (#2140): its dependents with row counts and blockers. STABLE, read only. Probed with the all zero id, which no row carries, so a successful probe refuses partner_not_found.

name: rename_partner_step_namespace
note: Rewrites a partner's formula columns for a step id rename (#1409). A WRITE. Probed with the all zero partner and no columns, which matches no row.

name: change_partner_uuid
note: Adds or removes a sub-account ID with the actor set for the partner_uuid_map triggers (#2135), behind POST and DELETE /api/partner-uuids. A WRITE. Probed with the all zero org, which holds no partner, so even a successful probe refuses partner_not_found and writes nothing. The Worker routes call it, so it must exist before that Worker deploys.

name: monitor_partner_page_ping
note: The partners page delivery monitor's send (#2135), called by the Worker's five minute cron. Sends a broadcast and writes no table row. Probed with the all zero org, which does not exist, so even a successful probe refuses organization_not_found and sends nothing.

name: record_held_click
note: Records a click claim buyer_click_send left held, so the partner page can list it (#1552). A WRITE, service_role only. Probed with every argument because PostgREST resolves a function by its argument names; as anon the call is refused before the body runs.

name: db_stall_snapshot
note: Called by the Worker the moment a post-response write times out (#2292, lib/db-stall-snapshot.ts) to record what every backend is doing during the stall. Security definer, reading every running query's first 300 characters, which can carry customer data, so it MUST be denied to anon (#762). If it is missing, every stall's snapshot is stored as failed and the cause goes unrecorded again. It takes no arguments, so an empty body names it.
